section_summary.extract_value: This subsection describes use of the Photographic Figure Rating Scale (PFRS) to measure actual–ideal weight discrepancy: participants selected current and ideal figures on a 10-point scale and discrepancy was computed as the absolute difference. The text notes that women completed the PFRS but men did not because no male version is available, and it references prior validations of the PFRS including in Malaysian women. No sample size, demographics, BMI assessment, survey method, or correlations are reported in this excerpt.
section_summary.evidence_source: Relevant sentences: 'Women completed the Photographic Figure Rating Scale (PFRS; ...). Participants were asked to select the figure that most closely matched their own body and the figure that they would most like to possess on a 10-point scale... A measure of actual-ideal weight discrepancy was computed as the difference between absolute current and ideal ratings... Men did not complete the PFRS because no male version of the PFRS is available.'
